dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify that importing the mcp-client-pat-* params with `value_wo_version=1` does not reset the live PATs to CHANGEME on the next apply (import records no version → null→1 change re-sends value_wo), and document/coordinate the required re-seed if it does.
evidence: The added comment claims value preservation: ssm.tf:199-201 'the provider stores only the version integer, never the secret value, so adoption records existence + type without reading the live token into state.'

infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md:89-93 confirms the clobber for exactly this scenario: 'On this first apply, value_wo_version goes absent → 1 for each migrated slot, so the provider sends value_wo = "CHANGEME" once and resets every migrated secret to the placeholder.'

The ticket (9350-174a-3320-4e33) fix precondition is stale: it says 'rebar_secrets already carries lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] } (ssm.tf:97-99), so adoption preserves the live values' — but the current resource uses value_wo, NOT ignore_changes.
dropped.finding: Importing the three mcp-client-pat-* parameters into a resource declared with write-only `value_wo="CHANGEME"` + `value_wo_version=1` will clobber the live operator-seeded PATs on the next apply: import records no `value_wo_version` in state, so the config `value_wo_version = 1` reads as a null→1 change and the provider re-sends `value_wo="CHANGEME"`, overwriting the live SecureString values.
scenarios: An operator runs `terraform apply` after this import lands; the three MCP PATs are reset from their live v1 operator-seeded values to the CHANGEME placeholder in AWS.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether a CHANGEME/reset MCP PAT would fail loudly or silently degrade MCP client auth after apply, and add a guard or coordinated re-seed step if silent.
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh:237: `[ -z "${value}" ] && return 0` — a blank slot's record is dropped entirely
ssm.tf:4-8 documents the CHANGEME fail-fast only for required secrets via user_data.sh; the MCP PATs are OPTIONAL (ssm.tf:63-66) and get no such guard

infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md:33-36: a reset CHANGEME value would materialize a bogus token or an omitted record, silently accepting/rejecting the wrong client digest set until an operator restarts rebar-mcp
dropped.finding: The unpopulated/reset MCP PAT slots fail silently rather than loud: fetch-secrets.sh reads them via get_param_optional and omits a blank/CHANGEME slot's record from mcp-static-tokens.json, so if the import+apply resets a PAT to CHANGEME the affected client loses auth with no fail-fast (unlike the top-of-file CHANGEME sentinel guard that protects required secrets).
scenarios: After a clobbering apply, the CHANGEME placeholder either registers as a bogus bearer digest or the record is omitted; MCP client auth silently misbehaves rather than failing the boot.

Ticket 9350-174a-3320-4e33 AC3 requires "live parameter VALUES are unchanged after adoption — verified by version number remaining at v1", which a CHANGEME re-push would violate by advancing to v2
dropped.finding: The adopting apply for the three write-only `value_wo` mcp-client-pat parameters may clobber the live operator-seeded token with the `CHANGEME` placeholder. An `import` does not populate the write-only `value_wo_version` into state, so the first post-import apply sees `value_wo_version` transition absent -> 1 — the exact condition the project runbook documents as causing the provider to re-send `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` and RESET the secret to the placeholder. The added comment only asserts the value is never READ into state, and is silent on whether the adopting apply WRITES CHANGEME back.
scenarios: Operator runs `terraform apply` to adopt the three imports; the first apply pushes `value_wo=CHANGEME`, overwriting the live copilot/codex/claude bearer PATs and advancing each to v2
MCP nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge `static` verifier then authenticates against the placeholder, breaking all three clients until re-seeded
